[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write

([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],

class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more

[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited multiplication and spectral items. On
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]])
put
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f:\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\},$$
a closed subspace of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$, and write
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$, $\Pi(0):=0$, so that
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}$ with $M_{\Pi}$ the bounded
multiplication by $\Pi$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]). Let
$c,\hbar>0$ with $c$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and $\hbar$ in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$, and for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $m\in\{\hbar k_{j},\ \hbar c|k|\}$
define
$$D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\ \textstyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}m(k)^{2}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty\},\qquad M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f:=mf .$$
Then for each such $m$:

(a) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on the
Hilbert space $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and it is the
restriction to $\mathfrak h$ of the self-adjoint multiplier $M_{m}$ on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]];

(b) its spectral projection-valued measure $E_{m}$ is given by
$$E_{m}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\bigr|_{\mathfrak h}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
and for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the outcome law $B\mapsto\|E_{m}(B)f\|^{2}$
is the push-forward of the finite measure $|f|^{2}\,d^{3}k\big|_{\mathfrak h}$
under $k\mapsto m(k)$; in particular for $m=\hbar k_{j}$ it is the push-forward
under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$ and for $m=\hbar c|k|$ it is the push-forward under
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]);

(c) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues: for no $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is
there a nonzero $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ with $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f=\lambda f$;

(d) for every unit $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ one has
$$\operatorname{Var}_{f}(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\|M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f\|^{2}-\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle^{2}>0;$$
consequently no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp $m$-value.

The identifications of $\mathfrak h$ and of these multipliers with physical
transverse photons, momenta or energies are not asserted here; they are a
separate model assignment outside this lemma.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

derivations.claim: [Number law] For $n\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace of $N$ at $n$ is $\{\psi\in D(N):N\psi=n\psi\}$; comparing coordinates with the definition $(N\psi)_{m}=m\psi_{m}$, this eigenspace equals $\iota_{n}(\mathfrak H_{n}^{+})$, the closed subspace of vectors supported in coordinate $n$. Hence by [F3] the spectral projection is $E_{N}(\{n\})=\Pi_{n}$, and for the one-photon state $\rho_{f}=T_{\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f}$ we get $\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(\{n\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{f}\Pi_{n})=\langle\Pi_{n}\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\delta_{n,1}$ by [F1]; since the atoms cover $\mathbb N$ and the law is a measure, $\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\mathbf 1_{B}(1)$ for every Borel set $B$. This proves (a).

[Frequency and energy laws] By [F5] the spectral measure of $H_f$ is $E(B)=\bigoplus_{n}E_{T_{n}}(B)$, and on the one-photon sector $\iota_{1}\mathfrak H_{1}^{+}$ it acts as $\iota_{1}E_{T_{1}}(B)\iota_{1}^{-1}$; since $T_{1}=\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ by [F4], the restriction is the spectral measure $E_{\varepsilon}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}}|_{\mathfrak h}$ of [F6]. Therefore $\mu^{H_f}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\langle E(B)\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\langle E_{\varepsilon}(B)f,f\rangle=\int_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k.$ The assigned frequency law is the push-forward under $k\mapsto c|k|$ by clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]]. These are the laws in (b), and they exist for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$.

[Push-forward integration and frequency and energy first moments] Let $
u_f(A):=\int_A\|f(k)\|^2\,d^3k$, a probability measure, and, for any real measurable $m$, let $\mu_m(B):=
u_f(m^{-1}(B))$. For an indicator $g=\mathbf 1_C$, the defining identity gives $\int g\,d\mu_m=\int g(m(k))\,d
u_f(k)$; linearity gives it for nonnegative simple $g$, and increasing simple approximation with [F8] gives it for every nonnegative Borel $g$. Applying this identity to $g(t)=t$ for the nonnegative frequency and energy maps gives the means in (b), finite under the stated first-moment condition. If also $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, the energy mean agrees with $\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}f,fangle$ by [F7]; the first-moment condition alone need not put $f$ in that operator domain.

[Momentum readouts and means] The same sector restriction gives $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\langle E_{m}(B)f,f\rangle=\int_{\{m\in B\}}\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ for $m(k)=\hbar k_j$, the push-forward under $k\mapsto\hbar k_j$. For the signed identity function, apply the push-forward integral identity proved in step 2.1 separately to its positive and negative parts; the assumed finite absolute first moment makes both integrals finite, so their difference is the mean stated in (c). If also $f\in D(M_m^{\mathfrak h})$, this mean agrees with $\langle M_m^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle$ by [F7] and the isometry of $\iota_1$. This proves (c).

[Strict positivity of the variances] By [F6] the multiplier $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues and every unit $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ has strictly positive finite energy variance; together with step 1.2 this gives the energy variance claim. The frequency law is the positive constant rescaling $\omega=E/\hbar$, so on the same domain its variance is $\hbar^{-2}$ times the energy variance and is strictly positive. The same clause of [F6] applied to $m=\hbar k_j$ gives strictly positive finite momentum-component variance whenever $f\in D(M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h})$. Hence no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp value of frequency, energy or any momentum component, and the assignments of the radiation postulate are spectral assignments. This proves (d).

[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove the frequency and energy claims in (b), step 3.1 proves (c), and step 4.1 proves (d). No step introduces a detector, a sampling model, a measured count or an empirical premise, which is (e).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$, sector
projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal creation and annihilation
operators $A_\pm(f)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] and
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit
vector $\varphi\in H$. Write $\varphi^{\otimes0}:=1\in\mathbb C$ and
$\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for
$n\ge1$, and define
$$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$
with the entry in coordinate $n$, extended linearly. Then:

(a) each $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; the family $(\varphi^{\otimes n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$
is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of
$F(\mathbb C)$ onto the closed subspace
$\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\varphi^{\otimes n}:n\in\mathbb N\}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(b) for every $\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\in F(\mathbb C)$ and every $n$,
$$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$
where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every
$\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with
$$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$

(c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$
and
$$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$
in particular for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the coherent vector
$\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] satisfies
$U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$;

(d) for the transverse case $H=\mathfrak h$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$, and a unit
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h\cap D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ (so that
$\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
and for every $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ with $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi\psi,U_\varphi\psi\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n|\psi_n|^{2}\Bigr)\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle N'\psi,\psi\rangle\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle ;$$
Already under $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing $\bar\varepsilon=\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle$, the finite spectral second moment is
$$\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\|\varepsilon\varphi\|^2+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^2.$$
If moreover $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$, the vector lies in $D(T_n^2)$ and this norm square equals the literal operator pairing below; then
$$\langle T_n\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle T_n^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle^{2}.$$

No physical interpretation of the isometry, of the vectors
$U_\varphi e_n$, or of the transferred operators is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], so that
$$F(H)=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)},\ \sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}$$
is a Hilbert space. For $n\in\mathbb N$ define
$$\Pi_n:F(H)\to F(H),\qquad \Pi_n\psi:=(0,\dots,0,\psi_n,0,\dots)$$
(the entry $\psi_n$ in coordinate $n$ and $0$ in all other coordinates). Then:

(a) each $\Pi_n$ is a bounded linear operator with
$\|\Pi_n\psi\|=\|\psi_n\|$ and $\|\Pi_n\|\le1$; it satisfies
$\Pi_n^2=\Pi_n$, $\Pi_n^*=\Pi_n$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and
$\Pi_n$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection of $F(H)$ onto the closed subspace
$\iota_n(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)})$ of vectors supported in coordinate $n$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) $\Pi_n\Pi_m=0$ for $n\ne m$, so the ranges are pairwise orthogonal and
$\|\Pi_n\|=1$ whenever $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ne\{0\}$ (which holds for
every $n$ when $H\ne\{0\}$);

(c) for every $\psi\in F(H)$ the series $\sum_{n}\Pi_n\psi$ converges in norm to
$\psi$, the expansion is orthogonal,
$$\psi=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\Pi_n\psi,\qquad \|\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\Pi_n\psi\|^2,$$
and the partial sums $\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n$ converge to the identity in the strong
operator topology, i.e. $\bigl\|\psi-\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n\psi\bigr\|\to0$ for
every $\psi\in F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(d) $\Pi_n=0$ as an operator if and only if
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\{0\}$; for $H\ne\{0\}$ no $\Pi_n$ vanishes.

No physical interpretation of the Fock space or of its sectors is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric
projections $P_+^{(n)}$ and Fock space $F(H)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Define the
number operator by
$$D(N):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (N\psi)_n:=n\psi_n .$$
Then:

(a) $N$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $F(H)$ with the displayed
domain; $N\ge0$ in the sense that $\langle N\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for
$\psi\in D(N)$, $N\Omega=0$, and $F_0$ is a core for $N$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) for every $n$, every nonzero $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ satisfies
$N\iota_n(u)=n\,\iota_n(u)$, and for $H\ne\{0\}$ the spectrum of $N$ is
$\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$;

(c) for $f\in H$ and $\psi\in F_0$ the core operators of
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] satisfy
$$N S_+(f)\psi-S_+(f)N\psi=S_+(f)\psi,\qquad N S_-(f)\psi-S_-(f)N\psi=-S_-(f)\psi ;$$

(d) $D(N)\subseteq D_1:=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, and for every
$\psi\in D(N)$,
$$\|N\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2,\qquad \langle N\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\|\psi_n\|^2 .$$

No physical interpretation of $N$, and no assertion about particle number
measurement, is made.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in
the measurement vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]].
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice, the choice hypotheses of
the cited readings ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared ideal total-number detector.** The **declared ideal
total-number detector** of the radiation sector is the declared ideal sharp
measurement with outcome set $\mathbb N$, outcome projection
$$P_{n}:=\Pi_{n}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the sector projections of the Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$; the family
$(\Pi_{n})$ consists of mutually orthogonal orthogonal projections with strong
sum $I$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clauses
(a),(b),(c)). Its **count law** in a declared radiation preparation $\rho$ is
the reading of clause (ii) of P2,
$$p_{n}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_{n}),\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}p_{n}(\rho)=1,$$
and its **number readout** is the assigned total-number observable $(N,1)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] read through the atom
law of P2. The conditional post-count state and the discarded-outcome state are
the Lueders updates of the measurement definition
([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]],
[[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]). The word "count" refers to
the quanta of the declared model; no laboratory counter, no absorption
process, no detection efficiency, no dark count, no dead time and no
background is declared here.

**(c) Declared ideal energy-window detector.** For a Borel set
$B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ read in joules the **declared ideal energy-window
detector of window $B$** is the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome
structure
$$\bigl(E_{H_f}(B),\ I-E_{H_f}(B)\bigr),$$
where $E_{H_f}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the assigned
free-field energy observable $(H_f,\mathrm J)$; its **window law** in the
preparation $\rho$ is $p_{B}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_f}(B))$ and its
complement probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I-E_{H_f}(B)))$, the reading
of P2. A finite-resolution detector is described by such a window or by a
declared family of pairwise disjoint windows covering $[0,\infty)$; the
statement that a laboratory spectrometer realizes a declared window, with what
resolution and calibration, is an identification under P7.

**(d) Declared analyser detection.** The **declared polarisation-analyser
detection** of the fixed propagation mode is the analyser family
$\{P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\}$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], read as a
declared ideal sharp measurement of the polarisation factor; its law and its conditional update are proved on this page. It detects the polarisation alternative of the model and is not a photon counter.

**(e) Repetition requires a separate sampling model.** The declaration of a
detector gives the outcome law of a single declared measurement. A prediction
for repeated trials, a count rate, or any statistical comparison with data
requires in addition a declared preparation-and-apparatus model and a sampling
model in the sense of P7 -- for instance an identically-and-independently
repeated preparation with a declared number of trials -- which this page does
not supply. A single measurement outcome law is not a frequency and no
frequency is asserted.

**(f) Destructive detectors are outside the declared class.** A
photoabsorption detector that destroys the absorbed quantum, and any detector
whose post-outcome state of the radiation field is not the Lueders update,
requires its own declared instrument, that is its own outcome effects together
with its own conditional updates (clause (v) of P3, clause (d) of the
measurement definition). No such instrument is declared on this page, and the
"blocked" outcome of the analyser is used only through its discarded-outcome
law.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (b)-(d) fix vocabulary and read the cited postulates;
they add no physical assumption beyond P1-P3, P7 and the radiation model, and
they assert no detection mechanism, no response function and no empirical
result. In particular, the declaration of an ideal counting model is not a
claim that any physical device counts photons, and the energy-window model is
not a claim that any physical spectrometer measures exact energy.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$, sector
projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal creation and annihilation
operators $A_\pm(f)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] and
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit
vector $\varphi\in H$. Write $\varphi^{\otimes0}:=1\in\mathbb C$ and
$\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for
$n\ge1$, and define
$$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$
with the entry in coordinate $n$, extended linearly. Then:

(a) each $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; the family $(\varphi^{\otimes n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$
is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of
$F(\mathbb C)$ onto the closed subspace
$\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\varphi^{\otimes n}:n\in\mathbb N\}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(b) for every $\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\in F(\mathbb C)$ and every $n$,
$$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$
where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every
$\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with
$$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$

(c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$
and
$$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$
in particular for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the coherent vector
$\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] satisfies
$U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$;

(d) for the transverse case $H=\mathfrak h$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$, and a unit
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h\cap D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ (so that
$\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
and for every $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ with $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi\psi,U_\varphi\psi\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n|\psi_n|^{2}\Bigr)\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle N'\psi,\psi\rangle\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle ;$$
Already under $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing $\bar\varepsilon=\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle$, the finite spectral second moment is
$$\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\|\varepsilon\varphi\|^2+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^2.$$
If moreover $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$, the vector lies in $D(T_n^2)$ and this norm square equals the literal operator pairing below; then
$$\langle T_n\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle T_n^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle^{2}.$$

No physical interpretation of the isometry, of the vectors
$U_\varphi e_n$, or of the transferred operators is asserted.

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].
For every $z\in\mathbb C$, the series $\sum z^n/n!$ converges absolutely.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the
Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse
subspace
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let
$M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write
$\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by
$\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$.
Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define
$$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$
and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put
$$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \psi_n\in D(T_n)\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and
$\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

(c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with
every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more
precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication
operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and
the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact.

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical
transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not
asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.

derivations.claim: [Number states] By [F1] each $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of the sector $\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$; by [F2] $N$ acts on it as $n$ times itself, so the number readout is $n$ with probability one by the atom law of P2 ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]]), and the count law of the declared detector is $p_{m}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}}\Pi_{m})=\langle\Pi_{m}Ue_{n},Ue_{n}\rangle=\delta_{mn}$. This proves (a).

[Poisson law] For the mode-coherent preparation $U\psi_{z}$ the count law is $$p_{n}=\langle\Pi_{n}U\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\langle U\Pi_{n}'\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\langle\Pi_{n}'\psi_{z},\psi_{z}\rangle=|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$ using [F1] for the sector transfer and the isometry, and [F3] for the coefficient.

[Poisson moments] Put $x:=|z|^{2}\ge0$. By [F5], $\sum_{n\ge1}n\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{x^{m}}{m!}=xe^{x}$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x^{2}e^{x}$, so the mean is $e^{-x}xe^{x}=x$ and the second moment is $e^{-x}(x^{2}+x)e^{x}=x^{2}+x$; hence the variance is $x$. For $z\ne0$ the law is supported on more than one value, so the preparation is not a number state. This proves (b).

[Energy means] The sector diagonality of $H_f$ and orthogonality of the sectors give, for the coherent preparation, $$\langle H_fU\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\,\langle T_{n}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}n\Bigr)\bar\varepsilon=|z|^{2}\bar\varepsilon,$$ where the middle identity is [F1] and [F4] and the last is the Poisson mean of step 2.1; the number-state value is the $n$-th instance of [F1]. The Poisson second number moment is finite by step 2.1, so [F1] places $U\psi_z$ in the actual domain of $H_f$ and justifies the graph-truncation passage. The mean exists because both sides are finite: $\bar\varepsilon<\infty$ by $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ and Cauchy-Schwarz, and $\sum_{n}n|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=x<\infty$. This proves (c).

[Energy variances] For the number state, $\|H_fUe_n\|^2=\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}$ by [F4], so the variance is $n(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2})$, which is strictly positive for $n\ge1$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]] (the energy multiplier has no eigenvalues, so $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}=\operatorname{Var}_\varphi(\varepsilon)>0$). For the coherent preparation, its Poisson second moment and [F1] give $U\psi_z\in D(H_f)$; the orthogonal-sector norm expansion therefore gives $$\|H_fU\psi_z\|^2=\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\bigl(n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr)=x\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+x^{2}\bar\varepsilon^{2},$$ using the Poisson first and second factorial moments of step 2.1; subtracting the square of the mean $x\bar\varepsilon$ from step 3.1 gives $x\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}$, which is strictly positive for $x=|z|^{2}>0$ because $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^{2}>0$: $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi$ vanishes only where $\varphi$ vanishes off the null set $\{k=0\}$, so a unit $\varphi$ cannot satisfy $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi=0$ in $\mathfrak h$. This proves (d).

[Full-sector Gibbs limitation and assembly] A trace-normalized density operator proportional to $e^{-\beta H_f}$ would require that operator to be trace class, which [F6] excludes for every stated $\beta$. This proves only the full-sector Gibbs limitation in (e). Steps 1.1 and 1.2 prove (a) and (b), steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c) and (d), and no step introduces a detector response, a sampling model or an empirical premise, which is (f).

citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), the radiation
extension postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], in the state
vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
observable and measurement vocabularies of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice
hypotheses of the cited spectral and measurement mathematics
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix angles
$\varphi,\theta,\theta'\in\mathbb R$ and write
$\psi_{\varphi}=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ and
$P_{\theta}$ for the analyser projections of the model. Then:

(a) the declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement with outcome structure $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$, the
outcome labels $+1$ and $-1$ naming the first and second projection, in
the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]:
$P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are bounded orthogonal projections with
$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$ and $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$;

(b) the spectral projection-valued measure $E$ of the bounded self-adjoint
operator $P_{\theta}$ (assigned with unit $1$; its values on the two outcomes
are $1$ and $0$, while the analyser labels are $+1$ and $-1$) satisfies
$$E(\{1\})=P_{\theta},\qquad E(\{0\})=P_{\theta}^{\perp},\qquad E(\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\})=0,$$
consequently the outcome law of the assigned sharp quantity $P_{\theta}$ in a
preparation $\rho\in D(V)$ is
$$p_{+1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}),\qquad p_{-1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp})=1-p_{+1}(\rho),$$
which is exactly the law of the declared analyser;

(c) for the linear-polarisation preparation $\psi_{\varphi}$ and a general
pure preparation with unit vector $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$,
$$p_{+1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{-1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{+1}(\psi)=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2};$$
for a statistical mixture $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ of preparations the law
is affine, $p_{+1}(\rho)=\sum_{n}w_{n}p_{+1}(\rho_{n})$;

(d) the law is invariant under the phase of the preparation and under the
phase of the analysed direction: $p_{+1}$ depends only on the rays
$[\psi_{\varphi}]$ and $[e_{\theta}]$, is $2\pi$-periodic in each argument, and
satisfies $p_{+1}(\theta,\varphi)=p_{+1}(\theta-\varphi,0)$;

(e) if $p_{+1}(\rho)>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $+1$ of the
analyser is $\rho_{+1}=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}/p_{+1}(\rho)$; for the pure
preparation $[\psi_{\varphi}]$ with $\cos(\theta-\varphi)\ne0$ it is the pure
state of the analysed ray $[e_{\theta}]$, and a second analyser at angle
$\theta'$ then gives the conditional probability
$\cos^{2}(\theta'-\theta)$ for the outcome $+1$. If the outcome is discarded,
the state is $\Phi(\rho)=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp}$;

(f) the assertions (a)-(e) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P3 and the
adopted model. They assert no dynamics, no laboratory polariser, no detector
efficiency, no loss, no sampling model and no empirical result; in particular
the fraction $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ is a model probability of the declared
ideal analyser, not a measured count.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

Applying [L1] with $E$ in place of $e_{1}$ gives $\|P_{\theta}E\|^{2}=\langle E,P_{\theta}E\rangle$; for the particular field datum $E=e_{1}$ this is $\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta$, and $I(e_{1})=\|e_{1}\|^{2}=1$ by [L1] and [L3]. This completes the announced computation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$, sector
projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal creation and annihilation
operators $A_\pm(f)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] and
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit
vector $\varphi\in H$. Write $\varphi^{\otimes0}:=1\in\mathbb C$ and
$\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for
$n\ge1$, and define
$$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$
with the entry in coordinate $n$, extended linearly. Then:

(a) each $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; the family $(\varphi^{\otimes n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$
is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of
$F(\mathbb C)$ onto the closed subspace
$\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\varphi^{\otimes n}:n\in\mathbb N\}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(b) for every $\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\in F(\mathbb C)$ and every $n$,
$$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$
where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every
$\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with
$$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$

(c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$
and
$$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$
in particular for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the coherent vector
$\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] satisfies
$U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$;

(d) for the transverse case $H=\mathfrak h$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$, and a unit
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h\cap D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ (so that
$\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
